findings.description: Source-reported SQL injections across the case, not modeled paths or total engagement findings

assumptions: Objective weight 5 represents assumed importance for demonstrated SQL-query execution; it is not customer supplied.
The patch candidate uses the existing assumed cost of 1 implementation unit, not measured customer effort.
Patching the represented SQL injection is modeled as removing e_sql_injection. This does not establish that one patch fixes all three reported injections. Legitimate workload effects are untested.
omissions: The fixture starts with reported authenticated application access after registration and token issuance. It is not a full Internet-to-data route.
The vulnerability represents one unnamed successful SQL injection, not all three combined. The source does not identify which registration mechanism or endpoint supplies this partial route.
Registration alternatives and token issuance remain supporting history outside the severable path. No account-removal, token-removal, or registration-policy candidate is modeled.
The other reported injections are not encoded as substitute edges or bypass hypotheses.
Linked-server queries and sensitive telecom-data retrieval remain source-reported case results in provenance. They are not assigned to the represented injection or counted as its objective.
No SQL principal, database role, permission binding, server identity, or linked-server topology is inferred.
The transcript's five additional SQL servers and the diagram's five reachable SQL servers do not establish an exact total or topology.
The roughly 68.5 million rows describe reported impact scope, not proof that every row was exfiltrated. SIM-swap prerequisites do not establish an executed SIM-swap attack.
Three SQL injections is a source-reported category count, not the total engagement finding count or a customer change count. No specific customer remediation actions are established.
This is a separate regression fixture, not part of the Fortune 600 demo input.
